rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is Paradise, the true abode of life because death and extinction cannot reach it; alternatively, it is itself life, an emphatic usage.
rows.anchor: أي : الجنة لهي دار الحياة الحقيقية لامتناع طريان الموت والفناء عليها أو هي في ذاتها حياة للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥayawān is a verbal noun from ḥayiya, used for a living being; its original form was ḥayyān, altered to avoid dropping one of the two alifs.
rows.anchor: والحيوان مصدر حيي سمي به ذو الحياة وأصله حييان فقلبت الياء الثانية واوا لئلا يحذف إحدى الألفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥayawān is more emphatic than ḥayāh because the faʿalān pattern conveys motion and agitation, fitting this context of emphasis.
rows.anchor: وهو أبلغ من الحياة لما في بناء فعلان من الحركة والاضطراب اللازم للحيوان ولذلك اختير على الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people understood, they would not prefer worldly life, whose basis is lifelessness and whose life is only a brief, vanishing accident.
rows.anchor: لما آثروا عليها الدنيا التي أصلها عدم الحياة ثم ما يحدث فيها من الحياة عارضة سريعة الزوال

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The world is mortality: God calls a disbeliever dead despite being alive; only one whom He revives with faith’s light is truly living.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن دار الدنيا لهي الموتان لأنه تعالى سمى الكافر وإن كان حيا بالميت

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The afterlife is the realm of spirits and the unseen kingdom, wholly alive; all its parts are living, hence it is called ḥayawān.
rows.anchor: الآخرة عبارة عن عالم الأرواح والملكوت فهي حياة كلها وإنما سماها الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says everything in Paradise, including its trees, fruit, rooms, walls, rivers, soil, and pebbles, is alive.
rows.anchor: إن الجنة بما فيها من الأشجار والثمار والغرف والحيطان والأنهار حتى ترابها وحصاها كلها حي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Paradise offers true life untouched by distress, calamity, illness, or death; knowing its worth would make people strive harder for it here.
rows.anchor: فالحياة الحقيقية التي لا تشينها الغصص والمحن والأمراض والعلل ولا يدكها الموت والفوت لهي حياة أهل الجنات والقربات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: What one misses of that life here cannot be recovered in the afterlife; the people of Hell neither truly live nor find the death they wish for.
rows.anchor: فمن فاتته لا يدركها في الآخرة ألا ترى أن من صفة أهل النار أن لا يموت فيها ولا يحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kashf al-asrar appends a Persian poem illustrating worldly striving through shifting images of a lion, wolf, partridge, and deer.
rows.anchor: غافل بي حاصل تاشند شربت مرادى آميزي ووتاكي ارزوي زي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written wāw in ribā either marks an emphatic spelling like ṣalāh and zakāh, or recalls its root rabā-yarbū, to increase.
rows.anchor: كتب بالواو للتفخيم على لغة من يفخم في أمثاله من الصلوة والزكوة أو للتنبيه على أصله لأنه من ربا يربو زاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribā is an uncompensated increase in an exchange: excess of the same kind in food or currency is ribā al-faḍl, while deferred exchange is ribā al-nasāʾ; both are forbidden.
rows.anchor: وهي الزيادة في المقدار بأن يباع أحد مطعوم أو نقد بنقد بأكثر منه من جنسه ويقال له ربا الفضل أو في الأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An increase taken without countervalue may grow in other people’s wealth but does not increase or receive blessing with God; God says He erases usury.
rows.anchor: لا يزيد عنده ولا يبارك له فيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret ribā here as a gift given in expectation of a better return: it is permissible, but earns no afterlife reward without seeking God’s face; it was forbidden to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد بالربا في الآية هو أن يعطي الرجل العطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a loan a gift or waiving the claim does not make a transaction God forbade lawful or stop it being ribā.
rows.anchor: لو قال المعطي للآخذ أنا لا أعطي هذا المال إياك على أنه ربا وجعله في حل لا يكون حلالا ولا يخرج عن كونه ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giver and receiver share the warning, except where the giver faces compelling necessity and can find no lender without a compensating return.
rows.anchor: وإلى أن المعطي والآخذ سواء في الوعيد إلا إذا كانت الضرورة قوية في جانب المعطي فلم يجد بدا من الأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakah here means either obligatory alms or charity; it is named for its growth and increase.
rows.anchor: مفروضة أو صدقة سميت زكاة لأنها تزكو وتنمو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s face means sincerely seeking His reward and pleasure, not another reward or people’s praise and reputation.
rows.anchor: تبتغون به وجهه خالصا أي : ثوابه ورضاه لا ثواب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muḍʿifūn are people granted multiplied reward, or those whose reward and wealth are multiplied through zakah’s blessing; the terms resemble words for the strong and wealthy.
rows.anchor: ذووا الأضعاف من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shifting from direct address to a report indicates that the promise applies to all accountable people until the Resurrection, not only the original addressees.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن الخطاب إلى الأخبار إيماء إلى أنه لم يخص به المخاطبون بل هو عام

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says multiplication is due to intending God’s face, not merely to giving zakah.
rows.anchor: قال سهل رحمه الله : وقع التضعيف لإرادة وجه الله به

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl describes bodily zakah as purification from sins and monetary zakah as purification from doubtful matters.
rows.anchor: وزكاة البدن في تطهيره من المعاصي وزكاة المال في تطهيره من الشبهات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Spending in God’s path purifies the self from worldly love; the Taʾwīlāt gives Abu Bakr as an example of giving wealth to purify himself.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن في إنفاق المال في سبيل الله تزكية النفس عن لوث حب الدنيا كما كان حال أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verses portray Abu Bakr giving to purify himself, with no favor to repay and solely seeking his Lord’s highest face—out of longing to meet Him.
rows.anchor: أي : شوقا إلى لقاء ربه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The sincere receive multiples beyond their hopes: their expectations are limited by present perspective, while God gives from timeless generosity without end.
rows.anchor: يعطون أضعاف ما يرجون ويتمنون لأنهم بقدر هممهم وحسب نظرهم المحدث يرجون والله تعالى بحسب إحسانه وكرمه القديم يعطي عطاء غير منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth is a recoverable loan in a person’s hand; only a fool would fail to save himself from lasting punishment with what will not remain his.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المال عارية مستردة في يد الإنسان ولا أحد أجهل ممن لا ينقذ نفسه من العذاب الدائم بما لا يبقى في يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guarantees compensation for what is spent; the Mathnawi depicts angels asking God to replenish spenders and bring loss upon misers.
rows.anchor: كفت يغمبركه دائم بهر ند دو فرشته خوش منادى ميكند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Bustan poem urges giving now, carrying provision forward, consoling the needy, and welcoming petitioners before one’s own day of need.
rows.anchor: ريشان كن امروز كنجينه ست كه فردا كليدش نه در دست تست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone brought people into existence from nothing, when they were nothing.
rows.anchor: أوجدكم من العدم ولم تكونوا شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provided food for people throughout their lives in this world.
rows.anchor: أطعمكم ما عشتم ودمتم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a warning to Meccan disbelievers: have they failed to see the outcome of their affairs? The implied subject is the abundance of God’s destruction, since كم cannot serve as subject.
rows.anchor: تخويف لكفار مكة أي : اغفلوا ولم يبين لهم مآل أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed earlier peoples include ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: مثل عاد وثمود وقوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qurūn is the population of the earth in one era; successive qurūn are its inhabitants across successive ages.
rows.anchor: والقرن اسم لسكان الأرض عصرا والقرون سكانها على الأعاصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause describes Meccans passing through the ruined peoples’ lands on their travels and seeing traces of destruction and ruined homes.
rows.anchor: الجملة حال من ضميرهم يعني أهل مكة يمرون في متاجرهم على ديار الهالكين وبلادهم ويشاهدون آثار هلاكهم وخراب منازلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction and its traces are proofs and admonitions for anyone able to reflect and learn.
rows.anchor: حججا ومواعظ لكل مستبصر ومعتبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should listen to God’s signs and admonitions with reflection, take heed, and stop their disbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: آيات الله ومواعظه سماع تدبر واتعاظ فينتهوا عما هم عليه من الكفر والكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Driving the water refers to driving water-bearing clouds, which is attributed to God; watering by rivers is attributed to people, though God causes the growth.
rows.anchor: والمراد سوق السحاب الحامل للماء لأنه هو الذي ينسب إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr al-ʿulūm takes seeing as knowing, but the author prefers literal sight because the process is perceptible and the verse ends by asking whether they see.
rows.anchor: حملا على المقصود من النظر أي : قد علموا أنا نسوق الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jurz is land whose vegetation has been entirely cut away by lack of rain or grazing, not inherently infertile land, since crops then emerge from it.
rows.anchor: لعدم المطر أو لغيره كالرعي لا التي لا تنبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By the water God brings out crops; zarʿ is originally a verbal noun used for the thing planted.
rows.anchor: وهو في الأصل مصدر عبر به عن المزروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock eat fodder, straw, leaves, and some grains; people eat food grains and fruit from the crop.
rows.anchor: كالتبن والقصيل والورق وبعض الحبوب المخصوصة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible provision should lead them to recognize God’s oneness, power, and favor, worship Him alone, and reject even angelic or human partners, let alone lifeless things.
rows.anchor: فيستدلون به على وحدته وكمال قدرته وفضله تعالى وأنه الحقيق بالعبادة وأن لا يشرك به بعض خلقه من ملك وإنسان فضلا عن جماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revival of barren land also demonstrates God’s power to restore people to life.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فيعلمون أنا نقدر على إعادتهم وإحيائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers told Meccan disbelievers that God would judge between them on a coming day, or grant believers victory over the polytheists and distinguish the sides.
rows.anchor: المؤمنين كانوا يقولون لكفار مكة إن لنا يوما يفتح الله فيه بيننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans asked when this judgment or victory would occur, impatiently mocking and denying the believers’ claim.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعوه يقولون بطريق الاستعجال تكذيبا واستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-fatḥ can mean the Resurrection, which removes doubt by opening what is closed, or a day of victory over enemies.
rows.anchor: يوم إزالة الشبهة بإقامة القيامة فإن أصله إزالة الإغلاق والإشكال أو يوم الغلبة على الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Resurrection Day, a disbeliever’s late faith cannot help because its time has passed; neither punishment nor the opportunity to present an excuse is delayed.
rows.anchor: فإن الإيمان يومئذ لا ينفع الكافر لفوات الوقت ولا يمهل أيضا في إدراك العذاب ولا في بيان العذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the day is a victory such as Badr, faith at the moment of being killed is despairing faith like Pharaoh’s as he drowned, and cannot stop the killing.
rows.anchor: كيوم بدر فإنه لا ينفع إيمانه حال القتل إذ هو إيمان يأس كإيمان فرعون حين ألجمه الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply does not answer their timing question literally; it stresses the less obvious point that faith then will not help and they will receive no respite.
rows.anchor: والعدول عن تطبيق الجواب على ظاهر سؤالهم للتنبيه على أنه ليس مما ينبغي أن يسأل عنه لكونه أمرا بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to disregard their denial; the Persian gloss describes turning away in contempt until the sword verse is revealed.
rows.anchor: بطريق اهانت از ايشان تامدن معلوم يعني تانزول آية السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to await victory over them and their destruction, assured by God’s truthful promise.
rows.anchor: النصرة عليهم وهلاكهم لصدق وعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expect victory over the Prophet or a worldly event such as his death that would free them; another explanation is that their conduct amounts to awaiting the punishment their sins entail.
rows.anchor: الغلبة عليك وحوادث الزمان من موت أو قتل فيستريحوا منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fulfilled His promise by granting victory to His servant and opening victory for the believers, fulfilling their hopes.
rows.anchor: وقد أنجز الله وعده فنصر عبده وفتح للمؤمنين وحصل أمانيهم أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding practical advice says fullness causes illness; if eating is necessary before cupping, first taste a little.
rows.anchor: وعلى الشبع داء إلا إذا كان به ضرر فليذق أولا شيئا قليلا ثم ليحتجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited regimen advises avoiding intercourse for a day and a night before and after cupping, and avoiding a bath on the day of cupping or bloodletting.
rows.anchor: وإذا أراد الحجامة يستحب أن لا يقرب النساء قبل ذلك بيوم وليلة وبعده مثل ذلك ولا يدخل في يومه الحمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bustan al-ʿĀrifīn advises avoiding salty foods, meat from the head, and dairy after cupping; vinegar, broth, and sweets are recommended.
rows.anchor: ولا يأكل رأسا ولا لبنا ولا شيئا مما يتخذ من اللبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author closes the medical advice by invoking God as healer and sufficiency.
rows.anchor: والله الشافي وهو الكافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God includes saying what befits Him, such as the declarations of divine oneness, praise, and greatness.
rows.anchor: بما هو أهله من التهليل والتحميد والتكبير ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr is bringing something to mind in the heart or in speech; remembrance after forgetting is the state of ordinary people, while sustained presence and mindfulness is the elite’s state.
rows.anchor: والذكر إحضار الشيء في القلب أو في القول وهو ذكر عن نسيان وهو حال العامة أو إذامة الحضور والحفظ وهو حال الخاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God continually in every time, place, and condition; in obedience seek sincerity and acceptance, in sin abstain and repent, in blessings give thanks, and in hardship be patient. Dhikr has no fixed limit or excuse except loss of reason.
rows.anchor: في جميع الأوقات ليلا ونهارا صيفا وشتاء وفي عموم الأمكنة برا وبحرا سهلا وجبلا وفي كل الأحوال حضرا وسفرا صحة وسقما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The states of people who remember God vary according to their forms of remembrance.
rows.anchor: وأحوال الذاكرين متفاوتة بتفاوت أذكارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lower form of remembrance stays on the tongue, without thought, heart-presence, spiritual intimacy, witnessing divine lights, or inward self-annihilation.
rows.anchor: فذكر بعضهم بمجرد اللسان بدون فكر مذكوره ومطالعه آثاره بعقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet urges familiarity with love’s sea and purity like a shell.
rows.anchor: صدف سان معدن در صفاباش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God free of what does not befit Him.
rows.anchor: ونزهوه تعالى عما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines sabḥ as swift motion through water or air; tasbīḥ is declaring God transcendent, originally rapid movement in worship, then generalized to worship by speech, action, or intention.
rows.anchor: السبح المر السريع في الماء أو في الهواء والتسبيح تنزيه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukrah and aṣīl mean the beginning and end of the day; mentioning both endpoints implies remembrance throughout the day, especially at these honored times.
rows.anchor: أي : أول النهار وآخره وقد يذكر الطرفان ويفهم منهما الوسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says angels take turns among people by night and by day, witnessing the two special periods.
rows.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ is singled out from other forms of remembrance because it is their central element, as a form of adornment.
rows.anchor: وإفراد التسبيح من بين الأذكار لكونه العمدة فيها من حيث أنه من باب التحلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith lists four phrases a person in major impurity should not omit: declaring God’s transcendence, praise, oneness, and greatness; the author infers that the ritually minor impure are even more entitled to say them.
rows.anchor: أربع لا يمسك عنهن جنب سبحان الله والحمدولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ is allowed in every state, though remembrance with ablution and purity is proper etiquette.
rows.anchor: فلا منع من التسبيح على جميع الأحوال إلا أن الذكر على الوضوء والطهارة من آداب الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kashf al-asrār interprets morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers, urging people not to let worldly work make them miss these prayers.
rows.anchor: وسبحوه أي : صلوا به بكرة يعني صلاة الصبح وأصيلا يعني صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith urges anyone able to avoid being overtaken by distractions from the prayers before sunrise and sunset to do so.
rows.anchor: من استطاع منكم أن لا يغلب على صلاة قبل طلوع الشمس ولا غروبها فليفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kashf al-asrār links dawn prayer to the angels’ witnessing in 17:78, and identifies the afternoon prayer as the middle prayer.
rows.anchor: لقوله تعالى : {إن قرءان الفجر كان مشهودا} (الإسراء : 78) يعني تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the earth cries out most intensely over unlawful blood, a bath after fornication, or someone sleeping on it before sunrise.
rows.anchor: ما عجت الأرض إلى ربها من شيء كعجيجها من دم حرام أو غسل من زنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distributes provision, sends blessings, and answers prayers between dawn and sunrise, so people should not be heedless during this honored hour.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى يقسم الأرزاق وينزل البركات ويستجيب الدعوات فيما بين طلوع الفجر وطلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith promises the reward of a complete pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage three times over to one who prays dawn in congregation, remembers God until sunrise, and then prays two rakʿahs.
rows.anchor: من صلى الفجر في جماعة ثم قعد يذكر الله تعالى حتى تطلع الشمس ثم صلى ركعتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufi practitioners gather for remembrance after dawn prayer until the sunrise prayer; remembrance then has a powerful effect on the soul and is preferred to recitation.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا لم يزل الصوفية المتأدبون يجتمعون على الذكر بعد صلاة الصبح إلى وقت صلاة الإشراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qunya says blessings on the Prophet, supplication, and tasbīḥ are better than Qurʾan recitation during times when prayer is prohibited.
rows.anchor: من أن الصلاة على النبي عليه السلام والدعاء والتسبيح أفضل من قراءة القرآن في الأوقات التي نهى عن الصلاة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Dāwūd contains no connecting letters, suggesting that God wholly detached him from the world and honored him with hidden and manifest graces; names and titles descend from heaven.
rows.anchor: أعطى الله تعالى داود اسما ليس فيه حروف الاتصال فدل على أنه قطعه عن العالم بالكلية وشرفه بألطافه الخفية والجلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḍl means increase; its indefinite form signals a kind of favor that set David above the prophets, while superiority in one respect can coexist with inferiority in another.
rows.anchor: والفضل الزيادة والتنوين للنوع أي : نوعا من الفضل على سائر الأنبياء مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor includes the mountains’ response, the birds’ subjection, and iron made pliable; these are special miracles, but do not exhaust David’s gifts, for God also gave him the Psalms.
rows.anchor: وهذا الفضل هو ما ذكر بعد من تأويب الجبال وتسخير الطير وإلانة الحديد فإنه معجزة خاصة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A questioner says that hearing the same remembrance as the spiritual traveler’s own would be an imaginary unveiling; a true unveiling hears a distinct remembrance from each thing.
rows.anchor: فمتى سمع السالك من الأشياء الذكر الذي هو مشغول به فكشفه خيالي غير صحيح يعني أنه خيال أقيم له في الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains’ agreement with David does not preclude their own distinct glorification, audible to him; alternatively, the wording means they traveled wherever he went, a miracle.
rows.anchor: لا يلزم من موافقة الجبال لداود أن لا يكون لها تسبيح آخر في نفسها مسموع لداود كما هي فيه والمعنى على الثاني سيرى معه حيث سار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayr is accusative, coordinated with faḍlan: God subjected the birds to David, so no omitted verb or estimated phrase meaning their glorification is needed, unlike al-Irshād’s parsing.
rows.anchor: ولا إلى تقدير المضاف أي : تسبيح الطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains and birds are addressed as rational beings; every animal and inanimate thing obeys God’s will and command.
rows.anchor: نزل الجبال والطير منزلة العقلاء حيث نوديت نداءهم إذ ما من حيوان وجماد إلا وهو منقاد لمشيئته ومطيع لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since even immobile rocks and fleeing birds respond to David, hardened hearts are more blameworthy when they reject remembrance and flee or attack gatherings of truth.
rows.anchor: فانظر إذ من طبع الصخور الجمود ومن طبع الطيور النفور ومع هذا قد وافقته عليه السلام فأشد منها القاسية قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāmī explains that David’s focused spirit transmitted glorification through his faculties and then to mountains and birds, reflections of those faculties; their praise’s reward therefore returned to him, not them.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان تسبيح الجبال والطير لتسبيحه لأنه لما قوي توجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet suggests that every voice, spoken or silent, is a voice from the Beloved; hearing it makes the listener inwardly silent.
rows.anchor: همه آوازها در يش حق باز اكر يدا اكر وشيده آواز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Līn means softness, first of bodies and by extension meanings; God made iron soft like wax, dough, or wet clay, shapeable by hand without heating or hammering.
rows.anchor: اللين ضد الخشونة يستعمل في الأجسام ثم يستعار للمعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, iron was soft relative to David’s exceptional bodily strength; he was powerfully strong though not bulky, as indicated by the description in Sūrat Ṣād.
rows.anchor: أو جعلناه بالنسبة إلى قوته التي آتيناها إياه لينا كالشمع بالنسبة إلى سائر قوى البشرية وكان داود أوتي شدة قوة في الجسد وإن لم يكن جسيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines sabagha as extending down to the ground; a complete, long coat of mail is sābighah, and the root is also used of an ample ablution or blessing.
rows.anchor: سبغ الشيء سبوغا طال إلى الأرض والنعمة انسبغت ودرع سابغة تامة طويلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David was the first to make coats of mail; armor had previously consisted of beaten flat iron plates.
rows.anchor: وهو عليه السلام أول من اتخذها وكانت قبل ذلك صفائح حديد مضروبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says David disguised himself to ask people’s opinion; an angel in human form faulted his use of the public treasury, prompting him to ask for a way to earn independently, whereupon God taught him armor-making.
rows.anchor: كان عليه السلام حين ملك على بني إسرائيل يخرج متنكرا فيسأل الناس ما تقولون في داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says David made one coat of mail daily, sold it for four or six thousand dirhams, kept two thousand for his family, and gave the rest to Israel’s poor.
rows.anchor: فكان يعمل كل يوم درعا ويبيعها بأربعة آلاف درهم أو بستة آلاف ينفق عليه وعلى عياله ألفين ويتصدق بالباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says David ate only from the earnings of his own hand.
rows.anchor: كان داود لا يأكل إلا من كسب يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that people of distinction should learn crafts: working with one’s hands does not lower rank but adds merit through humility and independence.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على تعلم أهل الفضل الصنائع فإن العمل بها لا ينقص بمرتبتهم بل ذلك زيادة في فضلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the best food a person eats is what comes from the work of their own hand; Saʿdī’s verse similarly praises craft and dignity over reliance on wealth.
rows.anchor: إن خير ما أكل المرء من عمل يده

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī’s Persian poem says to teach a craft and preserve dignity: a purse of silver and gold empties, but a craft keeps earning.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt says sard first meant stitching rough, thick material such as leather, then came to mean linking iron and weaving coats of mail. A maker was called sarād or zarād, and linked speech is also called sard.
rows.anchor: والسرد في الأصل خرز ما يخشن ويغلظ كخرز الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sard also means joining speech continuously, but such speech is acceptable only when it does not impair understanding.
rows.anchor: وسرد كلامه وصل بعضه ببعض وأتى به متتابعا وهو إنما يكون مقبولا إذا لم يخل بالفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David should weave the armor economically, keeping its rings proportionate; he should not spend all his time on the craft, only enough to provide strength, and devote the rest to worship.
rows.anchor: اقتصد في نسجها بحيث تناسب حلقها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The softening of iron signifies the softening of David’s heart; the full coats are profound judgments flowing from his heart through his tongue.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى إلانة قلبه والسابغات الحكم البالغة التي ظهرت ينابيعها من قلبه على لسانه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The command to measure the linking signifies speaking wisdom in a measure suited to people’s understanding.
rows.anchor: الحديث بأن تتكلم بالحكمة على قدر عقول الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet warns against offering fine points of wisdom to those unable to understand, like scattering jewels before a donkey.
rows.anchor: نكته كفتن يش كفهمان زحكمت بيكمان جوهرى ند ازجواهر ريختن يش خرست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural command addresses David and his household because the obligation applies generally.
rows.anchor: خطاب لداود وأهله لعموم التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous work is sincere work, free from ulterior motives.
rows.anchor: عملا صالحا خالصا من الأغراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees what they do and will not let any worker’s deed go unrewarded; this explains the command or why it must be obeyed.
rows.anchor: لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم فأجازيكم عليه وهو تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الامتثال به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya interprets the command as referring to every outward and inward faculty, each of which should perform the act of servitude suited to it and for which it was created.
rows.anchor: إلى جميع أعضائه الظاهرة والباطنة أن تعمل في العبودية كل واحدة منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baṣīr perceives every existent through sight; one who knows this name monitors every movement and stillness, avoiding what God forbids and not neglecting what He commands.
rows.anchor: والبصير هو المدرك لكل موجود برؤيته ومن عرف أنه البصير راقبه في الحركات والسكنات حتى لا يراه حيث نهاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this divine name’s special effect is success: reciting it one hundred times before Friday prayer opens inward sight and guides speech and action, though people remain fallible.
rows.anchor: وخاصية هذا الاسم وجود التوفيق فمن قرأه قبل صلاة الجمعة مائة مرة فتح الله بصيرته ووفقه لصالح القول والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying reports that David once prayed for wrongdoers not to be forgiven, from religious zeal; after his own lapse, he prayed for sinners to be forgiven.
rows.anchor: كان داود عليه السلام يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says that after David’s repentance, people, jinn, and birds gathered; when birds heard his voice but sensed his changed state, they flew away. God explained this estrangement as the effect of his lapse, unlike the intimacy of obedience.
rows.anchor: اجتمع الإنس والجن والطير بمجلسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet urges people to move only by God’s command and keep watch over obedience, since a step against His command brings a sharp reckoning.
rows.anchor: قدم نتوان نهاد آنجاكه خواهى بفرمان رو بفرمان كن نكاهى كه هر كاو نه بامر حق قدم زد
